newsitem.title: CANADA: ACI agrees to biennial Int'l congress after 2001.
newsitem.headline: ACI agrees to biennial Int'l congress after 2001.

text.p: The governing council of Association Cambiste Internationale (ACI) agreed to change its international congress from an annual event to once every two years after 2001, ACI secretary general Heering Ligthart said Saturday.
Addressing the general assembly of the 39th annual gathering of ACI - The Financial Markets Association in Toronto, Ligthart said there would be a greater emphasis on regional meetings.

The calender for future international congresses showed the event moving to Geneva in 1998, Jakarta in 1999, Paris in 2000 and Singapore in 2001. The congress will then skip two years and is expected to be held in the Middle East or Africa in 2003.
A regional Arab Congress is planned for Lebanon later this year, while a Pan-American congress is scheduled to return to Canada in 2000.
ACI's second emerging markets congress will take place in Jakarta in 1998.
